purpose: Close ASVS V9.2.3 by giving each of the four fixture-contour consumers its own audience and requiring it, so a token minted for one is refused by the others. Reachability was established first: nothing in this repository mints these tokens, and nothing in it sets the variables that enable the contour. No minting helper is added. No production deploy.
requiredInvariants: Reachability was established before anything was changed, and it produced two facts the record did not have: nothing in this repository mints a token carrying testAccess, owner or tokenType - every occurrence is a consumer - and the three variables that enable the contour are set nowhere in the tree. Both are stated in the evidence rather than used to argue the requirement away.
The env gate is not treated as compliance. Being switched off by default bounds exposure; it does not make a service accept only tokens intended for it, which is what the requirement asks.

No control is loosened. Every existing purpose claim each consumer checked - testAccess, owner, sub, email, role, tokenType - is still checked; the audience requirement is added alongside, never instead.
Audience and type are checked together, so a token carrying the right audience under the wrong type is refused rather than inspected further, and a mutation of either is caught on its own.

No minting helper is added. Introducing a first-party way to issue a credential that four surfaces trust would be a larger decision than the one this closes; the negative cases mint their own claims inline and need nothing in the tree.

Signature and algorithm stay with each caller, because each surface resolves its own secret. A test asserts the arrangement instead of re-testing the crypto: all four consumers still go through the shared verifier, which refuses any header algorithm other than HS256.

The named cost: a fixture token minted before this, by whatever mints them, stops being accepted, because it carries no audience. This is the fail-closed direction the owner accepted for cabinet cookies in #4787 and no transitional window is offered, for the same reason - a check that accepts tokens without an audience is not checking.
No database schema change, no migration, no new dependency. No production, REG.RU, DNS or credential mutation. The 1C, marketing and presentation contours are not touched.

The cryptographic inventory moves by exactly one scanned file and zero call sites, which is what adding a module that contains no cryptography should do. It is regenerated rather than edited, and the diff was checked rather than assumed.
acceptance: The full replay matrix in both directions across all four services: a token for any one is refused by each of the other three, nine of nine assertions.
A missing audience, a foreign audience and an empty audience are each refused at every service.
The right audience under four wrong types is refused at every service.
The RFC 7519 list form of aud is accepted only when it names the service, and an empty list is refused.
Absent claims are refused rather than treated as unconstrained.
Four mutations are caught: removing the audience check, removing the type check, giving two services the same audience, and one consumer ceasing to require its own.
Removing one consumer's audience requirement revokes V9.2.3 at the matrix level - applied 331 / rejected 1, PASS back to 104 - so the PASS is held by condition rather than asserted.
The matrix rebuilds at applied 332 / rejected 0: PASS 104 to 105, FAIL 115 to 114, NOT_ASSESSED unchanged at 38.
The new spec runs in CI and is registered as executed, not excluded; web tsc --noEmit exit 0.
